transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Aisha Kumar: Aisha here, thanks.
[00:06] Tom Reynolds: Tom — Product.
[00:08] Felipe Costa: Felipe, backend.
[00:10] Daniel Ortega: Daniel from Redwood SE.
[00:12] Nora Li: Nora, security.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda is output contract, SDK snippet review, and next steps. We also want to confirm the staging tests.

[02:15] Maya Chen: Recap from last week — you all ran the initial integration and saw a handful of schema mismatches, right Aisha?
[02:23] Aisha Kumar: Yeah. Mostly around optional fields turning up null and the enum mapping. For example the payment_method field came back as 'card' vs 'CARD' so our parser blew up.
[02:37] Daniel Ortega: That's predictable — transcription and casing, different models may have different canonicalization. We'll send a canonicalization helper in the SDK.

[05:10] Tom Reynolds: On the UI side, we also rely on a strict array ordering for line_items. When that was missing we had to fallback and re-sort which added latency. Any chance we can pin the response ordering or return an index?
[05:25] Daniel Ortega: We can include an index in the structured output, yes. Two ways: modify prompt to assert ordering, or use a post-process SDK shim that inserts indices based on parsing. The SDK approach is safer for now.

[08:40] Felipe Costa: One practical problem: function-calling for our reconciliation tool needs typed outputs — we can't have freeform strings for amounts. Does Redwood's function-calling support typed numbers and nested objects?
[08:52] Daniel Ortega: Yes, the SDK supports function-calling with a JSON schema. You define the function signature and Redwood will attempt to return structured JSON. There are edge-cases where the model strings a number, like "twelve"; the SDK includes coercion helpers.

[11:03] Aisha Kumar: We also noticed that sometimes the model streams partial JSON then finishes; our parser chokes on the intermediate fragment. Is there a recommended streaming-safe parser?
[11:16] Maya Chen: Good call. For streaming we recommend accumulating the final JSON in the SDK and exposing two hooks: on_partial and on_final. on_partial gets raw token chunks (useful for UI progress), on_final yields a validated JSON object. We'll add example code.

[14:30] Nora Li: From security side, KMS integration for customer-managed keys is hard requirement. We need to see key rotation docs and audit logs.
[14:43] Priya Singh: I'll send the SOC2 artifact and the security checklist after this call.
[14:49] Maya Chen: We'll put the KMS doc in the next step list. Also we support envelope encryption — we'll include the pattern we used for another fintech POC.

[18:00] Daniel Ortega: I'm going to walk through the SDK snippet now — bear with me I'll paste the example. The recommended flow: create client with credentials, register function schema, call generateWithFunction('reconcile', payload) and then validate outputContract against JSON schema.
[18:16] (typing/some crosstalk)
[19:05] Daniel Ortega: Example note: use strict mode = true to fail fast on schema mismatch in staging. That will make mismatches explicit rather than silently coercing.

[22:10] Felipe Costa: Can we see an example of a nested object schema? For example payments -> card -> expiry_month as integer.
[22:23] Daniel Ortega: Yes. I'll include an example where expiry_month is integer, expiry_year integer, amount is number with two decimals. I'll also include unit tests that assert types and that malformed values raise ValidationError.

[25:40] Aisha Kumar: We had a test that showed 0.8% of requests returned amounts as strings with commas, like "1,234.56". That breaks our parser.
[25:53] Daniel Ortega: We'll add a normalization utility to the SDK to strip commas and coerce numeric strings. Also will add a metric to telemetry: schema_coercion_rate.

[29:02] Tom Reynolds: On cost and latency — our concern is the tail latency when you add the validation/rewrites. How much is added per request?
[29:14] Daniel Ortega: Validation is cheap on CPU for the JSON sizes you're describing (~<2KB). The bigger tail comes from model latency. We'll schedule a dedicated bench to measure 95th and 99th percentile with you using the same prompt templates and sequence lengths.

[32:55] Maya Chen: Quick note — for the bench run we'll need the real-ish workload distribution: short confirmations, medium reconciliation, and long multi-line invoices. Aisha, can you export a sample distribution?
[33:06] Aisha Kumar: Yes I can. 70% short, 25% medium, 5% long is roughly what we saw. I'll upload the anonymized payloads.

[36:20] Nora Li: About audit logs — we need request IDs tied to KMS key IDs and a retention window. Is that in Redwood's private offering?
[36:33] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated and Private support extended audit logs. We'll generate a sample log snippet showing request-id, model used, latency, and key-id. We'll include that in the security docs.

[39:50] Felipe Costa: Error cases — if the SDK can't coerce a value, what's the recommended pattern? Return an error payload or fallback to best-effort?
[40:03] Daniel Ortega: Best practice: in staging use strict mode and fail hard so you uncover schema issues. In prod you can set fallback_policy = "best_effort" which will populate an errors array in the structured output with a code and human message. We'll show both patterns.

[43:10] Aisha Kumar: A quick real example — when the payment_method enum mismatch happened it returned 'cc' and our code mapped that to null. We want an example mapping table in the SDK where teams can register synonyms.
[43:25] Daniel Ortega: We'll add a synonyms map in the SDK that is configurable per-deployment; I'll include it in the PR.

[46:00] Tom Reynolds: About function-calling retries — if the model returns an invalid JSON we want an automatic retry with a slightly different temp and a prefixed instruction to be more literal. Is that supported?
[46:15] Daniel Ortega: The SDK supports retry policies. We can implement a validator middleware that, on JSON parse error, rewrites the prompt with 'return strictly valid JSON matching schema' and retries once or twice. We'll provide that middleware example.

[49:40] Maya Chen: OK, to recap — Redwood -> share SDK PR with typed function-calling + unit tests; share KMS and SOC2 artifacts; schedule bench run. StratoPay -> run SDK in staging and surface mismatch examples and workload distribution. Any objections?
[49:58] Nora Li: No objections, just please include rotation and key-id in the audit sample.
[50:08] Aisha Kumar: We'll try the snippet this week.
[50:20] Maya Chen: Great. We'll sync next Tuesday same time. Thanks everyone.
[50:30] (call ends, recording stops)
